spans.s:
Tābuva is the name in the Atharvaveda^1 of a remedy against
snake poison. The Paippalāda recension has Tāvuca instead.
Weber^2 thinks that the original form was Tāthuva, from the
root sthā, ‘stand,’ and that it meant ‘stopping’; but this is
hardly probable.^3
1) v. 13, 10.
2) Proceedings of the Berlin Academy,
1896, 681.
3) Barth. Revne del'Histoire des Religions,
39, 26. Cf. Whitney, Translation of
the Atharvaveda, 244; Bloomfield,
Hymns of the Atharvaveda, 428.
